issues.t: Lighting wiring harness can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Lights that flicker or quit, a burning plastic smell, or smoke from the wiring.
issues.why: Some lighting wiring harnesses were not soldered properly and can short circuit, which can lead to a fire. Kia recalled these cars to repair the wiring.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning or see smoke, stop the car and have it inspected before driving again.

issues.sym: Brake lights that don't come on, cruise control that won't turn off or won't engage, or the shifter staying stuck in Park.
issues.why: The switch that senses the brake pedal can malfunction. Other systems rely on it, so a failure also affects cruise control and the shift lock. Kia recalled these cars to replace the switch.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Ask someone to confirm your brake lights work; if they don't, get it fixed before driving in traffic.

issues.t: Headliner plate can come loose when the curtain airbag deploys (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs in normal driving.
issues.why: A plate in the headliner area could break free if the side curtain airbag goes off and strike someone inside. Kia recalled these cars to fix it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Clunk in the steering from a worn coupler
issues.sym: A click or clunk you feel in the steering wheel, mostly when turning at low speed or while parked.
issues.why: A small rubber coupler between the electric power steering motor and the steering shaft wears out and lets parts knock together. Kia issued service bulletins for it.
issues.next: Have the steering coupler inspected. It is a modest repair, but have the rest of the steering checked at the same time to rule out something more serious.

issues.t: ABS control unit can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: An ABS warning light, a burning smell, or smoke from the engine bay, possibly even when the car is parked and off.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control unit can develop an internal electrical short that may lead to an engine-compartment fire. Kia told owners to park outside until the recall repair is done.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls now. Park outside and away from buildings until a dealer completes the repair.

issues.t: Overheated catalytic converter can damage the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, rattling from the exhaust, loss of power, trouble reaching highway speed, or engine knocking.
issues.why: Very high exhaust temperatures can break down the catalytic converter. That can cause abnormal combustion that damages pistons and, in some cases, a fire. Kia recalled these cars to update the engine software and replace damaged parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the car feels choked or knocks, get it to a Kia dealer soon rather than driving on it.

issues.sym: A deep knocking from the engine that gets louder with speed, low oil level, a flashing check engine light, or the car going into reduced-power mode.
issues.why: Rod bearings in these engines can wear out early and lead to engine failure. Kia added knock-sensing software that detects early bearing wear and puts the car in limp mode, and longer engine coverage was tied to that work and a class settlement.
issues.next: If you hear knocking, pull over and do not keep driving. Ask a Kia dealer whether your VIN has the knock-sensor software and extended engine coverage, and keep your oil-change receipts.

issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the hood, warning lights, or engine noise before trouble starts.
issues.why: Kia recalled these cars because a fire could start in the engine compartment while driving. Dealers inspect and repair affected engines.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal can bend or break (recall)
issues.sym: A pedal that feels bent, loose or broken, and difficulty getting the car to accelerate.
issues.why: The accelerator pedal arm could bend or break, making it hard to control speed. Kia recalled these cars to replace the pedal.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the pedal feels damaged, don't drive the car until it is replaced.

issues.sym: Clunking or looseness in the steering, or steering that feels disconnected.
issues.why: A part inside the steering gear can come loose and let the pinion gear separate, which could cause loss of steering. Kia recalled these cars to inspect and fix or replace the steering gear.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and do not delay the repair if the steering feels loose.

issues.sym: An airbag warning light, or no warning at all.
issues.why: The airbag control unit can lose contact with the front crash sensors, so the front airbags might not go off in a crash. Kia recalled these cars to fix it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the repair done promptly. Don't ignore an airbag warning light.

issues.t: Airbag control unit cover can disable the airbags (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light on the dash.
issues.why: The cover of the airbag control unit can damage a circuit inside it, which can shut the airbags off. Kia recalled these cars to inspect and fix the unit.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the airbag light is on, get the car checked soon.

issues.t: Piston ring defect causing oil burning and engine damage (recall)
issues.sym: High oil consumption, blue smoke from the tailpipe, knocking or rattling noises, the oil pressure light, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Piston oil rings in some engines were not made correctly. They can damage the cylinders, burn oil and lead to engine failure or a fire. Kia recalled these cars to inspect engines, add noise-monitoring software and replace damaged engines.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Check the oil level often until the recall work is done, and stop driving if the engine knocks or the oil light comes on.

issues.t: Theft risk on key-start models without an immobilizer
issues.sym: A broken steering column cover or ignition cylinder, or the car being stolen or tampered with.
issues.why: Many key-start Souls were built without an engine immobilizer, which made them a target for a widely shared theft method. Kia offers a free software upgrade for eligible cars and help with a steering wheel lock for cars that can't take the software.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer whether your VIN qualifies for the free anti-theft upgrade. A steering wheel lock adds extra protection.

issues.t: Transmission oil pump controller can overheat and burn (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, smoke, or transmission warnings; the car may be parked when it happens.
issues.why: The electronic controller for the transmission oil pump can overheat and start a fire. Kia told owners to park outside until the recall repair is done.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls now. Park outside and away from buildings until a dealer completes the repair.

issues.sym: The gauge display goes dark, so speed, warning lights and tire pressure alerts don't show.
issues.why: A fault in the instrument cluster can blank the display. Kia recalled these cars to fix it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for open recalls. If the gauges go dark, get it repaired before regular driving.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may deploy unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; an airbag warning light may appear.
issues.why: The side curtain airbags could go off without a crash, which could injure people inside. Kia recalled these cars to fix it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the repair done promptly.

issues.t: 2.0L engine can burn oil, knock and fail
issues.sym: The oil level drops fast between changes, the engine knocks or rattles, then it may lose power or shut off and not restart.
issues.why: Piston rings that do not seal let oil into the combustion chambers; the engine runs low on oil and the rod bearings wear until a rod lets go.
issues.next: Check the oil now and have the engine looked at before driving far, and ask a dealer to run the VIN for engine campaigns, because a seizure can happen without warning.

issues.t: IVT automatic hesitates, slips or loses drive
issues.sym: The car hesitates or will not move off when you press the pedal, the engine revs while the car barely accelerates, or drive is lost suddenly at speed. Some owners find no drive or reverse at all, and the transmission ends up replaced.
issues.why: The Intelligent Variable Transmission belt-and-pulley unit and its control software can mishandle engagement on these cars. Kia's service campaign updates the transmission control module logic and tells dealers to replace the IVT if the update does not cure it.
issues.next: Stop driving if the car loses drive or will not hold a gear in traffic, and have it towed. Ask a Kia dealer whether the transmission control module update has been done on your VIN and keep records, since the powertrain warranty may cover a replacement.
